title: Structured Home Visit Protocol for CHWs
implementation_guidance: Implement a structured home visit protocol for post-discharge patients that includes: 1) Conducting an initial visit within 72 hours of hospital discharge; 2) Performing a standardized home environment assessment focusing on medication storage, fall risks, and accessibility barriers; 3) Reconciling discharge medications with all medications in the home, including over-the-counter products; 4) Using teach-back method to verify understanding of discharge instructions and warning signs; 5) Establishing a communication bridge between the patient and primary care provider with specific documentation templates; and 6) Scheduling follow-up visits at 7, 14, and 30 days post-discharge with decreasing intensity based on patient stability. The protocol should include clear escalation pathways for clinical concerns and standardized assessment tools for common post-discharge issues.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day hospital readmission rates, improved medication adherence, increased attendance at follow-up appointments, earlier identification of post-discharge complications, and enhanced patient satisfaction with care transitions.
target_population: Adults recently discharged from hospital, particularly those with complex medication regimens, limited health literacy, or history of readmissions
citation: Kangovi S, Mitra N, Grande D, et al. Patient-centered community health worker intervention to improve posthospital outcomes: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Intern Med. 2014;174(4):535-543. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.14327
